newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch airforce flie aid to Rwanda and Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Dutch airforce flie aid to Rwanda and Zaire.

text.p: More aid flights with relief goods destined for Rwanda and Zaire are expected to leave the Netherlands soon, said Major Breemans, official spokesman for the transport squadron of the Dutch Airforce.
Already three flights have left Eindhoven airport, where the transport squadron is based, for Uganda. The aid flights were on behalf of Unicef, the United Nation's childrens' foundation.
They were operated by McDonnell Douglas DC-10 freighter aircraft owned by the Dutch Airforce and flown in the first two weeks of November, added Major Breemans.

The flights left Eindhoven for Copenhagen initially where the Unicef headquarters are based. The aircraft were then loaded with humanitarian relief goods including blankets, clothes, plastic sheets, food and medicines.
Using the DC-10 meant Entebbe airport was the only suitable airport for the aircraft, he added. Unicef then took over and trucked the cargo to Rwanda and Zaire.
Two DC-10 aircraft and two Hercules C130s, owned by the Dutch Airforce, are based at Eindhoven Airport.

The Dutch Airforce operate relief flights on request and it has also carried out operations on behalf of the Red Cross and Medecine sans Frontiere, said Major Breemans. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
